# `docker run` options in runlike 2.0

All 103 options of `docker run` in Docker CLI v29.9.3 (source: the [docker run reference for Docker CLI v29.9.3](../spec/v29.9.3/container_run.md)).

- **Reproduced**: runlike reads the value from `docker inspect` and prints the
  option. Tested by recreating a container on a real Docker daemon and comparing
  both containers' inspect output.
- **Reproduced (tested on saved data)**: same, but the test machines cannot
  create such a container (Windows-only options, kernel features they lack), so
  the test uses inspect output saved from a real daemon.
- **Folded into other options**: the option is expanded by the docker client
  and stored as other settings, which runlike prints instead.
- **Not recoverable (client only)**: the option only changes what the docker
  client does while it runs; the daemon never stores it.
- **1.6.3**: whether the last Python release handled it. The notes say how.

| Option | Platform | runlike 2.0 | 1.6.3 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--add-host` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python prints each host entry but does not shell-quote it. |
| `--annotation` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores annotations. |
| `-a, --attach` | any | Reproduced | no | Python only uses AttachStdout to decide on --detach and never prints -a. |
| `--blkio-weight` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python 1.6.3 ignores it. |
| `--blkio-weight-device` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores per-device block IO weights. |
| `--cap-add` | Linux | Reproduced | yes | Python prints each added capability. |
| `--cap-drop` | Linux | Reproduced | yes | Python prints each dropped capability. |
| `--cgroup-parent` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the parent cgroup. |
| `--cgroupns` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the cgroup namespace mode. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): stored only when given, so every stored value is printed. |
| `--cidfile` | any | Reproduced | no | Printed when set. docker run fails if that file already exists, so remove it or change the path before running the copy. |
| `--cpu-count` | Windows | Reproduced | no | Windows-only; the CLI refuses it against a Linux daemon. Live Windows round trip; the Windows daemon discards --cpu-percent when --cpu-count is set. |
| `--cpu-percent` | Windows | Reproduced | no | Windows-only; the CLI refuses it against a Linux daemon. Live Windows round trip (range 1-100; discarded next to --cpu-count). |
| `--cpu-period` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the CFS period. |
| `--cpu-quota` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the CFS quota. |
| `--cpu-rt-period` | Linux | Reproduced (tested on saved data) | no | Needs a kernel with real-time group scheduling; Docker Desktop refused --cpu-rt-runtime on create. |
| `--cpu-rt-runtime` | Linux | Reproduced (tested on saved data) | no | Docker Desktop refused it on create (kernel does not support CPU real-time scheduler). |
| `-c, --cpu-shares` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores CPU shares. |
| `--cpus` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the CPU limit. |
| `--cpuset-cpus` | Linux | Reproduced | yes | Python prints it when set. |
| `--cpuset-mems` | Linux | Reproduced | yes | Python prints it when set. |
| `-d, --detach` | any | Reproduced | yes | Python prints --detach=true when stdout is not attached. |
| `--detach-keys` | any | Not recoverable (client only) | no | Only affects the attaching client; the daemon does not store it. |
| `--device` | any | Reproduced | yes | Python prints host:container[:perms] for each device. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): class/GUID and IDType://ID values are stored as given and round-trip. |
| `--device-cgroup-rule` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores device cgroup rules. |
| `--device-read-bps` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores block IO limits; stored as bytes per second. |
| `--device-read-iops` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores block IO limits. |
| `--device-write-bps` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores block IO limits. |
| `--device-write-iops` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores block IO limits. |
| `--dns` | any | Reproduced | yes | Python prints each DNS server. |
| `--dns-option` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores DNS options. |
| `--dns-search` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores DNS search domains. |
| `--domainname` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the NIS domain name. |
| `--entrypoint` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python keeps only the first entrypoint element and drops the rest ([#141](https://github.com/lavie/runlike/issues/141)). |
| `-e, --env` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python leaves out image env values, but in stdin mode it repeats them. |
| `--env-file` | any | Folded into other options | no | The file is read by the client; its entries land in Config.Env and come back as --env. |
| `--expose` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python prints --expose for every unpublished port, including ports the image already exposes. |
| `--gpus` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Stored as a device request. Python 1.6.3 ignores it. |
| `--group-add` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores supplementary groups. |

| `--health-interval` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores health checks; stored in nanoseconds. |
| `--health-retries` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores health checks. |
| `--health-start-interval` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores health checks; stored in nanoseconds. |
| `--health-start-period` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores health checks; stored in nanoseconds. |
| `--health-timeout` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores health checks; stored in nanoseconds. |
| `--help` | any | Not recoverable (client only) | no | Prints usage; nothing to recover. |
| `-h, --hostname` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python always prints the hostname, even the auto-generated one taken from the container ID. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): under --network host the daemon keeps the ID-prefix host name. |
| `--init` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores --init; the field is null unless the flag was given. |
| `-i, --interactive` | any | Reproduced | no | Python never prints -i. |
| `--io-maxbandwidth` | Windows | Reproduced | no | Windows-only. Live Windows round trip. |
| `--io-maxiops` | Windows | Reproduced | no | Windows-only. Live Windows round trip. |
| `--ip` | any | Reproduced | no | Python never prints the static IPv4 address. |
| `--ip6` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python prints the first network's static IPv6 address, whatever network it belongs to. |
| `--ipc` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the IPC mode. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): stored only when given, so every stored value is printed. |
| `--isolation` | Windows | Reproduced | no | A Linux daemon accepts only 'default', so only Windows containers carry a real value. A Windows daemon stores its own default (process on Server, hyperv on client Windows); runlike leaves it out only when it equals docker info Isolation, so --stdin prints it. process and hyperv round-trip live on create; starting hyperv is untested (the test VM has no usable hypervisor). |
| `-l, --label` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python leaves out image labels but quotes values with plain single quotes, which breaks on a quote in the value; stdin mode repeats image labels. |
| `--label-file` | any | Folded into other options | no | The file is read by the client; its entries land in Config.Labels and come back as --label. |
| `--link` | any | Reproduced | yes | Python prints legacy links on the default bridge. |
| `--link-local-ip` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores link-local addresses. |
| `--log-driver` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python prints the driver whenever it is not json-file, so a daemon default such as local is printed too. |
| `--log-opt` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python prints log options unquoted. |
| `--mac-address` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python reads Config.MacAddress, which the pinned API no longer returns, so a set MAC is lost. |
| `-m, --memory` | any | Reproduced | yes | Python prints the limit in bytes. |
| `--memory-reservation` | Linux | Reproduced | yes | Python prints the soft limit in bytes. |
| `--memory-swap` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the swap limit. |
| `--memory-swappiness` | Linux | Reproduced (tested on saved data) | no | cgroup v2 daemons discard it with a warning (seen on Docker Desktop), so only cgroup v1 hosts store it. |
| `--mount` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python turns every mount into -v, losing tmpfs, mount options, propagation and volume drivers. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): bind, volume and npipe round-trip; tmpfs mounts are refused. |
| `--name` | any | Reproduced | yes | Python prints the name unless --no-name is given. |
| `--network` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python uses only NetworkMode and loses extra networks, aliases and per-network settings. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): the default network is nat, left out; none, host and nat networks with aliases round-trip. |
| `--network-alias` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores network aliases. |
| `--no-healthcheck` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores health checks. |
| `--oom-kill-disable` | Linux | Reproduced (tested on saved data) | no | cgroup v2 daemons discard it with a warning (seen on Docker Desktop). |
| `--oom-score-adj` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the OOM score adjustment. |
| `--pid` | Linux | Reproduced | yes | Python prints the PID mode when set. |
| `--pids-limit` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the PID limit. |
| `--platform` | any | Reproduced | no | Printed only when the image's platform differs from the daemon's native one. |
| `--privileged` | Linux | Reproduced | yes | Python prints --privileged when set. |
| `-p, --publish` | any | Reproduced | partly | Python reuses the first binding's IP and port for a port's later bindings. |
| `-P, --publish-all` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores -P and prints the random ports it produced instead. |
| `--pull` | any | Not recoverable (client only) | no | Controls the client's image pull; not stored. |
| `-q, --quiet` | any | Not recoverable (client only) | no | Silences the client's pull output; not stored. |
| `--read-only` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the read-only root filesystem. |
| `--restart` | any | Reproduced | yes | Python prints the policy and on-failure retry count. |
| `--rm` | any | Reproduced | yes | Python prints --rm when set. |
| `--runtime` | Linux | Reproduced | partly | Python always prints the runtime, including the daemon default runc. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): none stored on create, io.containerd.runhcs.v1 set on start; both left out. |
| `--security-opt` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores security options. |
| `--shm-size` | Linux | Reproduced | partly | Python always prints the size, including the 64 MB default. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): stored only when given (0 otherwise), so every stored value is printed. |
| `--sig-proxy` | any | Not recoverable (client only) | no | Behaviour of the attached client; not stored. |
| `--stop-signal` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the stop signal. |
| `--stop-timeout` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the stop timeout; the field is set only when the flag was given. |
| `--storage-opt` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores storage options; Docker Desktop stored and started size=1G. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): size=30G round-trips. |

| `--tmpfs` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores --tmpfs mounts, which are not in Mounts. |

| `--ulimit` | Linux | Reproduced | no | Python ignores ulimits. |
| `--umask` | Linux | Reproduced | no | New in API 1.56; stored as a decimal number (0027 is 23) and printed back in octal. |
| `--use-api-socket` | any | Folded into other options | no | Docker turns it into a socket mount plus DOCKER_CONFIG; runlike prints --use-api-socket back when both are present. The credentials Docker copied in cannot be read back. |

Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): C:\ paths, drive targets and named pipes (\\.\pipe\...) round-trip; the daemon stores binds in a random rotation of the given order. |
| `--volume-driver` | any | Reproduced | no | Python ignores the volume driver; only the local driver is available on the test VMs. |
